precepts.text: After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do. Why did God say that? Because we learned the Egyptian customs while we were there. The same way here in America you learned the names of the week, named after their gods; that is idolatry. Everything you learned in Egypt, forget it. It is going to be the same when we are delivered up out of here.
precepts.point: Guess what: it is the same thing with us here in America. A lot of you have food, you are full, you are comfortable. Well, for now.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
It was not just that the Egyptians fed us. Everything we learned, we learned from the Egyptians back then. So when we came out of Egypt, God said: “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do”.

Why did God say not to do after the doings of Egypt? Because we learned the Egyptian customs while we were there, the Egyptian names of the week. It is the same way here in America: you talk about Monday and Tuesday and all of that, days named after their gods, and all that is idolatry.

So God says, everything you learned in Egypt, forget it. The people who longed for the fish and the melons of Egypt were still holding on to Egypt in their hearts. And it is going to be the same thing when we are delivered up out of here, out of spiritual Egypt: everything we learned from this land, we will have to leave behind.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech. Molech worship dealt with children and the womb, and we became bullheaded and did it anyway.
precepts.point: The children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, served Baalim, and forsook the Lord God of their fathers which brought them out of Egypt. They served Baal and Ashtaroth. That stubbornness is our history and why we are in captivity.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.” Molech worship went along with the fertility gods: it dealt with children, with the womb. That is what we were doing, and it is exactly what God told us not to do. We became bullheaded and stubborn and started worshipping the devil. That is how Israel “forsook the Lord, and served Baal and Ashtaroth.”

Stubbornness runs through this whole history. “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loveth danger shall perish therein.” So we have to prophesy against the idolatry and come up out of this foolishness: Christmas, Valentine's Day, which a lot of our people celebrated. It has nothing to do with us. God did not give it to us.

“Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn”. That is why God's laws are taught without going to the left or the right: we know how we got over here, through stubbornness. If we want to be delivered, we have to wake up.

It is how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down unto them; they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” When there is no judge, no leader, in place, they go back to their lonesome: the officer's not here, the captain's not here, the Deacon's not here, the Bishop ain't here. If you can't uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, the same judgment is your future. Stubborn goes back to bullheaded, and bullheaded goes back to Baal.

“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.” Stubbornness is idolatry; it is satanic worship. So many think they are not dabbling in the mystic arts, but when you are stubborn and rebellious, you are: “sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone”.

precepts.text: The nakedness of thy father and mother thou shalt not uncover; incest is against the law of the Most High.
precepts.point: The firstborn bare Moab, father of the Moabites, and the younger bare Benammi, father of the Ammonites, unto this day. In this teaching those nations are identified with the peoples known today as the Chinese and the Japanese.

note.label: Genesis 19: The Destruction of Sodom

precepts.why:
Lot’s daughters thought Sodom had been the whole world and “there is not a man in the earth to come in unto us”, so they made their father drink wine and lay with him, and “he perceived not when she lay down, nor when she arose.” Do not take any wayward idea from this. “The nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother, shalt thou not uncover.” Uncovering the nakedness of thy father is against the laws of the Most High. It was unlawful then and it is unlawful now.

Out of it came two nations: the firstborn bare Moab, “the father of the Moabites unto this day”, and the younger bare Benammi, “the father of the children of Ammon unto this day.” Those nations are identified with the peoples known today as the Chinese and the Japanese.

precepts.text: After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do; Egypt did not keep the covenant of circumcision.
precepts.point: The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do”. The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and Egypt did not keep the covenant.

The covenant was between the Lord and Israel. Moses, come out of Egypt, had left his son after the doings of the land of Egypt, and the Lord met him and sought to kill him for it.

precepts.text: After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do; Israel had to be commanded away from what was learned there.
precepts.point: The Lord put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel and sanctified his people with these laws; these laws make us special, going back to Deuteronomy 7 and 6, how he separated us. Do not follow the customs and fashions of the heathen.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
After Israel came out of Egypt, we had learned heathen practices there, such as drinking blood. So the Lord said, “I am the Lord your God. After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do: neither shall ye walk in their ordinances.”

Drinking the blood of animals was an Egyptian custom tied to their idols, and the blood-drinking customs of the Hamitic nations continue to this day. Israel had to be commanded away from what was learned there; that is why the statute against eating blood had to be spoken.

precepts.text: Obey His voice and He is an enemy to thine enemies; the nations of Canaan and their gods were to be overthrown, not learned from.
precepts.point: Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind: not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High.

note.label: Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do

precepts.why:
The land of Canaan was full of idols, and the Most High told Israel before they got there what to do about them. “if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.” His Angel would go before them and bring them in unto the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, and cut them off.

The charge in Canaan was plain: “Thou shalt not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do after their works: but thou shalt utterly overthrow them, and quite break down their images.” The nations of Canaan and their gods were to be overthrown, not learned from. That is what “after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do” means.

And the blessing for obeying: “ye shall serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread, and thy water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of thee.”

precepts.text: Be not conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.
precepts.point: Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind: not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High.

note.label: Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do

precepts.why:
In Egypt the children of Israel served the gods of Egypt, dressed like Egyptians and were fully engulfed in the Egyptian way of life; Moses himself was raised as an Egyptian in the house of Pharaoh. The Most High told them to leave all of that back in Egypt: “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.”

Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind. “be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” Not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High.

The same word stands for us. When the Most High redeems us out of this captivity, many of the customs we learned here will be cut off, because they are not coming into the kingdom.

precepts.text: Fornication that one should have his father's wife; the law of Leviticus 18:8 was being broken in the days of the apostles.
precepts.point: This very sin was reported among the Corinthians, a fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife. The law had already forbidden it, and it was being done in Egypt and Canaan; that is why the Most High opened the chapter the way He did.

note.label: Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do

precepts.why:
“The nakedness of thy father’s wife shalt thou not uncover: it is thy father’s nakedness.” That is the stepmother. The wicked mind reasons that she is not the biological mother, so it is fine to lust after her; the scripture says no, that is wicked.

This very sin was reported among the Corinthians: “It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father’s wife.” The law had already forbidden it, and it was being done in Egypt and Canaan; that is why the Most High opened the chapter the way He did, and why it was still being broken in the days of the apostles.

precepts.text: The law of her separation: she shall be put apart seven days.
precepts.point: A woman put apart for her uncleanness is a woman in her menstrual cycle. A man must wait the appointed seven days, and if the issue runs beyond, wait again; Leviticus 15 details these laws of uncleanness, taught in the previous class.

note.label: Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do

precepts.why:
A woman “put apart for her uncleanness” is a woman in her menstrual cycle. Leviticus 15 details these laws of uncleanness: “if a woman have an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be put apart seven days: and whosoever toucheth her shall be unclean until the even.”

So a man must wait the appointed seven days, and if the issue runs beyond, wait again. Thou shalt not approach unto her as long as she is put apart.

precepts.text: Thou hast slain my children and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire; that is what giving seed to Molech means.
precepts.point: The abortions of today are no different. The Most High is bringing spirits into the earth, and the child is slain so the parents can go on living as they please; that is the same sacrifice unto Molech, and it is wickedness.

note.label: Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do

precepts.why:
Passing seed through the fire to Molech was child sacrifice: the nations slew their newborn children and offered them to that god, and Israel learned it from them. Ezekiel testifies of Jerusalem: “thou hast taken thy sons and thy daughters, whom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured. Is this of thy whoredoms a small matter, That thou hast slain my children, and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire for them?”

That is what giving seed to Molech means: slaying the children of the Most High and delivering them to the fire.

The abortions of today are no different. The Most High is bringing spirits into the earth, and the child is slain so the parents can go on living as they please; that is the same sacrifice unto Molech, and it is wickedness.

precepts.text: The nakedness of thy sister thou shalt not uncover; the curse repeats the law already given.
precepts.point: This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

precepts.why:
“Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father, or the daughter of his mother.” This is not a new law spoken on the mount; it goes back to Leviticus 18, where the nakedness laws were first given: “The nakedness of thy sister, the daughter of thy father, or daughter of thy mother, whether she be born at home, or born abroad, even their nakedness thou shalt not uncover.”

The curse repeats the law already given. Whether the sister is born at home or born abroad, of the same father or of the same mother, her nakedness is not to be uncovered. The man who does it is cursed, and all the people say Amen.

precepts.text: The abominations Judah practiced were the very things the law commands Israel not to do.
precepts.point: They built high places, images, and groves on every hill, and there were also sodomites in the land, doing according to the abominations of the nations cast out before them.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not lie with mankind, as with womankind: it is abomination.”

The abominations Judah practiced were the very things the law commands Israel not to do. When the scripture says there were sodomites in the land, and that they did “according to all the abominations of the nations which the Lord cast out before the children of Israel”, this is the abomination it means. The nations were cast out for these things, and Judah took them up.

precepts.text: The manner of the heathen is the immoral laws and spiritual idolatry that we followed back then and still follow today.
precepts.point: We get judged because we do not keep the Most High's laws, the same then as today; they had not walked in His statutes but had done after the manners of the heathen around about them.

note.label: Ezekiel 11: This City Shall Not Be Your Cauldron

precepts.why:
“ye shall know that I am the Lord: for ye have not walked in my statutes, neither executed my judgments, but have done after the manners of the heathen that are round about you.” The law had warned them: “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do: neither shall ye walk in their ordinances.”

The manner of the heathen is the immoral laws and spiritual idolatry that we followed back then and still follow today. We get judged because we do not keep the Most High's laws, the same then as now; so He delivers us into the hands of strangers, the nations, and judges us in the border of Israel, that we may know that He is the Lord.

precepts.text: You shall not do after the doings of the land of Egypt or of Canaan, which is why the idols of Egypt point to the immoral laws that follow in that chapter.
precepts.point: They rebelled and would not cast away the abominations of their eyes nor forsake the idols of Egypt, so He said He would pour out His fury, but He wrought for His name's sake that it should not be polluted before the heathen.

note.label: Ezekiel 20: I Will Not Be Inquired Of

precepts.why:
When He brought them out of Egypt the Most High said, “Cast ye away every man the abominations of his eyes, and defile not yourselves with the idols of Egypt”. What are the idols of Egypt? Leviticus 18 tells you: “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do: neither shall ye walk in their ordinances.”

The doings of Egypt are the immoral laws laid out in the rest of that chapter. The idols of Egypt and the doings of Egypt point to the same thing: the abominations of their eyes that they were commanded to cast away.

They rebelled and “would not hearken”; they did not cast away the abominations of their eyes, “neither did they forsake the idols of Egypt”. So He said He would pour out His fury upon them in the midst of Egypt, but He “wrought for my name’s sake, that it should not be polluted before the heathen”. And the doings of spiritual Egypt today still apply: they are not to be done.

precepts.text: It is forbidden to let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech or to profane the name of the Most High, the cult sacrifice they were committing.
precepts.point: They defiled His sanctuary the same day and profaned His sabbaths, for when they had slain their children to their idols they came the very same day into His sanctuary to profane it, one foot in and one foot out, exactly as we still do when we sin all night and sit in church the next morning.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Among the abominations Ezekiel is to declare: they “caused their sons, whom they bare unto me, to pass for them through the fire, to devour them.” The law forbade exactly that: “thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.”

That is the cult sacrifice they were committing, and it broke both halves of the commandment. They passed their seed through the fire, and they profaned His name: “when they had slain their children to their idols, then they came the same day into my sanctuary to profane it”. Blood in their hands, and the same day in His house.

One foot in and one foot out. It is exactly as we still do when we sin all night and sit in church the next morning. They defiled His sanctuary and profaned His sabbaths in the midst of His own house.

precepts.text: The nakedness of thy father's wife thou shalt not uncover; you profane the Most High's holy name when you go against this commandment.
precepts.point: They lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar and drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god.

note.label: Amos 2: Because They Sold the Righteous for Silver

precepts.why:
“a man and his father will go in unto the same maid, to profane my holy name”. The law says, “The nakedness of thy father’s wife shalt thou not uncover: it is thy father’s nakedness.” You profane the Most High's holy name when you go against this commandment.

There were men even in that time going in unto their father's wife, and you may find a TV show today promoting that behavior.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

precepts.why: The abominable. “That ye commit not any one of these abominable customs”: don’t keep any one of these abominable customs. Let’s read some of them that some of us, here and online, might be involved with.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

precepts.why: “The nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother”: to have sex with your mom is abominable; the father’s wife is your stepmother; then your sister. “Thy son’s daughter, or of thy daughter’s daughter”: your grandchild. Everybody’s family got that nasty granddaddy you don’t want your kids staying with. Then your stepsister, your aunts, your daughter-in-law, your sister-in-law. “A woman and her daughter”: some of you are dealing with the mama and the daughter both; the Bible says that is abominable. “Neither shalt thou take a wife to her sister”: having two women, a ménage, a threesome; you can’t do that. “As long as she is put apart for her uncleanness”: you’re supposed to wait seven days; don’t run the red light, and you women be giving into that thing. “Lie carnally with thy neighbour’s wife”: that’s adultery. “Pass through the fire to Molech”: what were they doing with their children? Killing them. The new word today is abortion; do not abort your babies, that is abominable. “Thou shalt not lie with mankind, as with womankind”: marriage helps, but if you know you are still battling with that same sex demon, don’t get married yet; get counselling, pray and fast, and get that demon out. “Neither shalt thou lie with any beast”: that’s bestiality, and it’s nasty; that’s abominable. Then, verse 30: keep mine ordinance.
